Subject: Post-call recap: vector dimensionality & initial fit signals

Hi Elena — great to connect today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery focused on semantic search fit:

Summary of what we heard from Searchlytics:
- Index size: ~120M docs, mixed short/long (snippets + long-form).
- Current embedding model: vendor-provided 512-d vectors with periodic weekly reindexes.
- Pain: drift over time (content skew), inconsistent recall on long-tail queries, and cost at scale.

Initial Redwood readouts / hypotheses:
- We saw promising nearest-neighbor density improvements with 768-d embeddings on similar datasets (higher MRR and recall@10), but dimensionality increases compute and storage cost.
- For your use-case (hybrid snippet+long), prefix/KV caching + per-query dimensionality selection could help (lower dims for short snippets, full dims for long contexts).

Attachments I shared: semantic-bench-results.csv (sample metrics), prompt-set-v1.txt (seed queries we used).

Recommended immediate next steps:
1) Share 2K representative queries + 2K doc samples (anon) so we can run a 1-week embed A/B (512 vs 768).
2) Redwood will run recall@10, MRR, mean cosine differences, index size estimates, and an initial drift projection.
3) We’ll draft a lightweight pilot SLA (attached) focused on throughput & SLOs for embedding refresh cadence.

Can you confirm timeline for data handoff? We can run an initial synthetic run on Monday if you can drop samples by EOD Friday.

Thanks — Sean

Elena — thanks, that timeline works. High-level answers to infra questions and the A/B plan below.

Quick infra/latency notes (empirical from two recent pilots):
- 512 -> 768 dims typically ~15-30% increase in storage depending on quantization; with 8-bit quantization and PQ, storage overhead can be reduced to ~8-12% vs dense float.
- 99th-pct latency: on x1 GPU-serving tier with optimized kernels we’ve seen cold 99th go from ~120 ms (512) to ~160–180 ms (768) under continuous-batch load; with KV caching for hot prefixes 99th drops to ~70–90 ms.

Planned A/B (what Redwood will run):
- Dataset: your 2K queries + 2K docs (anonymized).
- Models to evaluate: redwood-embed-semantic-768-v2, redwood-embed-semantic-512-stable, & a production baseline (vendor-512).
- Metrics: recall@1/5/10, MRR, mean avg precision, cosine histogram, per-query latency distribution, index size (GB), dimensionality breakdown.
- Drift check: compute embedding drift (cosine shift) between weekly snapshots simulated over 3 months using content perturbations.
- Acceptance criteria: +7% recall@10 vs baseline OR +0.04 MRR with <=25% storage delta (post-quantization).

I’ve attached the semantic-bench-results.csv with a toy run we did on a sample dataset — look for the recall and MRR rows. Also linking a short notebook in Drive for how we compute drift.

Next steps: 
- Elena: confirm samples by Fri EOD PT.
- Infra: if you can share an S3 bucket read-only path for samples it speeds onboarding.
- Redwood: we’ll aim to deliver A/B results in ~5 business days after data receipt, with a short tech-readout doc and recommended pilot configuration.

—Sean

Quick engineering note on evaluation sensitivity — copied from our bench playbook:

1) Sample representativeness: please ensure the 2K docs include at least 20% long-form (>1k tokens) and 25% short snippets (<128 tokens). Dimensionality gains often manifest specifically on long contexts.
2) Prompt-set: we need edge-case queries in prompt-set-v1.txt (already attached in Sean’s mail). Those drive MRR lift more than median-query tests.
3) Drift simulation: our script perturbs entity mentions and topical priors; we’ll produce a cosine-drift per-week chart. Threshold of concern: median cosine shift >0.06 (we flag for reindexing).

Operational recommendation for pilot config:
- Run both models in productionized shadow mode for two weeks; route 5–10% of traffic to 768 variant for true online signals.
- If storage delta post-quant is >18% we recommend compressed ANN index (PQ with 64 clusters) to keep costs bounded.

I’ll prep the evaluation runbook and include expected SLO impacts (storage, 95/99 latency).

Karthik
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
